subject: c10-it

weightage.label: Part B Unit 1: Digital Documentation (Writer, Ch 6–8)
Part B Unit 2: Electronic Spreadsheet (Calc, Ch 9–12)
Part B Unit 3: Database Management System (Base, Ch 13–17)
Part B Unit 4: Maintain Healthy, Safe and Secure Working Environment (Ch 18–20)

note: Official 2026-27 theory marks: Part A Employability Skills 10 and Part B subject-specific skills 40 (Writer 8, Calc 10, Base 12, workplace health/safety/security 10). The other 50 marks are practical: practical examination and viva 30, project work 10, portfolio/practical file 10. The portfolio is specified to contain printouts of at least 5 problems each from Writer, Calc and Base.

reference.label: Communication cycle
reference.text: Sender → Message → Channel → Receiver → Feedback. Keep the communication clear, complete, concise, correct and considerate.

reference.label: ICT security
reference.text: Remember the three basic security goals: confidentiality, integrity and availability; use strong, unique passwords and safe digital practices.

reference.label: Writer: styles and TOC
reference.text: Heading styles → hierarchy → Table of Contents generation → navigation. Update the TOC after structural changes.

reference.label: Writer: images
reference.text: Insert → modify/resize/crop → arrange/anchor/align → choose text wrapping. Keep the image relationship with surrounding text intentional.

reference.label: Writer: review
reference.text: Prepare document → record changes/comments → review → accept/reject → compare when needed.

reference.label: Calc: Goal Seek
reference.text: Specify the desired result and target cell; Goal Seek adjusts the chosen input cell to reach that result.

reference.label: Calc: cell references
reference.text: Relative A1 changes when copied; absolute $A$1 stays fixed; mixed $A1 or A$1 fixes one dimension.

reference.label: Calc: linking data
reference.text: Use references between sheets/documents and distinguish ordinary references from hyperlinks or external/registered data links.

reference.label: Base: database structure
reference.text: Database → tables → fields/columns + records/rows. Primary key uniquely identifies a record; foreign key connects related tables.

reference.label: Base: relationships
reference.text: Common relationship types are 1:1, 1:N and N:M. Use appropriate keys and maintain referential integrity.

reference.label: Base: queries, forms and reports
reference.text: Query = retrieve/filter data; Form = enter/view/edit data; Report = formatted presentation/output of selected data.

reference.label: Workplace safety
reference.text: Identify hazards → assess risk → apply control measures. In an emergency, protect people, raise the alarm/call for help and evacuate or assist safely according to procedure.

mistakes: Do not study IT only as theory: the official assessment includes 50 practical marks, so practise Writer, Calc and Base directly.
In Calc, check whether a reference should be relative, absolute or mixed before copying a formula.
In Base, define keys and relationships before building dependent queries, forms and reports.
For Writer, distinguish a style, template, table of contents, comment and tracked change; they solve different problems.
Keep the portfolio and project work organised throughout the year rather than trying to reconstruct them immediately before assessment.
order: Build Employability Skills steadily in short sessions because all five Part A units contribute to the theory paper.
Practise Writer hands-on, especially styles, images, TOC, templates and review features.
Spend substantial practical time on Calc: scenarios/Goal Seek → macros → linking → sharing/review.
Then master Base: tables/keys → relationships → queries → forms/reports.
Keep workplace safety, project work and portfolio work active throughout the year.
